messages:
maria: Heads-up — onboarding a new community model (weights at s3://redwood-models/community/xl-variant-v2) and I'm seeing weird prompt-boundary tokens when using our chat templates. Not sure if it's tokenizer config or model-side BOS/EOS.

sam: Can you paste a minimal repro? is it happening only with the chat template or also plain generation?

maria: Plain generation too. quick test:
```
# local repro
from transformers import AutoTokenizer
t = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('s3://redwood-models/community/xl-variant-v2/tokenizer')
print(t.encode("\nUser: Hello\nAssistant:"))
```
Result: leading token id 1 (we expect BOS 0) and there's an extra trailing EOS when we pass messages through our chat templating.

jon: hmm. Two places to check: tokenizer.json special tokens mapping and our serving config that can force-add bos_token_id/eos_token_id. Are we accidentally double-inserting?

li: I saw this before with a different LLM where `add_prefix_space` + byte-level splitting made the first token differ. Also check `tokenizer.pad_token` vs `eos_token` — some tokenizers use the same id and that confuses our prompt-boundary heuristics.

sam: @maria can you `t.special_tokens_map` and `t.all_special_ids`?

maria: sure — output: `{'bos_token': '<s>', 'eos_token': '</s>', 'unk_token': '<unk>'}` and `all_special_ids: [0, 2, 3]` where 0==BOS, 2==EOS, 3==UNK. But the encode() I showed gave `[1, ...]` for first id. So either our local tokenizer build is mismatched to the model weights or the tokenizer vocab index shifted.

jon: Did we mount the tokenizer vocab from the right bucket prefix? We had a bug where tokenizer files lived under `tokenizer/` vs `tokenizer-vocab/` and the runtime fell back to a different tokenizer. Check the model manifest `model.yaml` for `tokenizer_files` path.

maria: model.yaml has `tokenizer_files: tokenizer/` and the bundle in S3 actually has `tokenizer-v2/`. Oof. That would explain it. I'll reupload the correct tokenizer bundle.

deploy-bot: model-upload: "xl-variant-v2" -> upload complete (s3://redwood-models/community/xl-variant-v2) by maria at 1767894500

li: Good catch. One more thing: our chat templating layer strips trailing whitespace and then appends `\nAssistant:`; if tokenizer expects a leading space for the assistant turn, token ids shift. Consider using `template_preserve_leading_space: true` in serving config for this model.

sam: For safety we should also add a validation rule in model onboarding: verify that `encode(template_prefix)` starts with BOS if model advertises a BOS. Quick lint: run `./tools/tokenizer_check --model s3://...` which compares model's special token ids vs tokenizer behavior.

maria: opening a small PR with two changes: fix tokenizer path in S3 + add a canned `tokenizer_check` step in onboarding CI. Will ping for review.

jon: If you can, include the minimal reproducer and the failing token ids in the PR description. Saves time.

maria: will do. thanks y'all :thumbsup:

sam: tiny nit — also add a note in the runtime config docs about `template_preserve_leading_space`; that bit keeps biting teams.

maria: added to checklist. closing once PR merges.

li: re: long-term: we probably need an automated unit test that exercises all chat templates for new models to catch these off-by-one token shifts before deployment.

maria: agreed — adding to backlog.

deploy-bot: deploy-status: PR #1723 created by maria (tokenizer path + onboarding check)

maria: pinging reviewers @sam @jon — thanks again.
